title: Nintendo's On The Hunt For A Digital Archivist To Preserve Its Rich History

Keep the past present.

With closing online storefronts, the move to digital media and the rise of streaming, there are few gaming industry topics more discussed right now than preservation. In short, this person would be responsible for ensuring that all things Nintendo are kept safely stored away and easily accessible.

title: Mini Review: Sonic Pico Park (Switch) - Charming Puzzle-Platformer Returns With A Nostalgic Co-Op Collab
summary:
(We) gotta go fast.

Pico Park is a fascinating success story for developer Shunsuke Miyake, who created the original game over a decade ago while working at Sega. A cute, minimalist and deceptively challenging puzzler, it exploded in popularity with the introduction of online co-op and a feature-packed sequel that was released on Switch in 2024.

This new spin-off takes the escalating challenge of multiple puzzle modes and invites Sonic and his ever-expanding menagerie of friends to the party. Available on both Switch 1 and 2, Sonic Pico Park takes the core mechanics of Pico Park and adds a suite of design features from the Blue Blur's 16-bit heyday.

title: Zelda: A Link Between Worlds Listed As 'Playable With NSO', But Let's Not Jump To Conclusions
summary:
An upcoming new library? Probably not...

Nintendo's official website for the Zelda series has updated its entry for A Link Between Worlds with a mysterious 'Playable with Nintendo Switch Online' icon, leading some to believe that it's a hint of an upcoming expansion to the paid service. However, we're not so sure.

The site is home to a series timeline, listing every mainline game from the NES original through to the Ocarina of Time remake. The likes of A Link to the Past, Link's Awakening and Oracle of Seasons are all marked with a 'Playable on NSO' button and, indeed, you can play all of them on the service. A Link Between Worlds has been locked to the 3DS since its launch back in 2013, however. Not only is it decidedly not playable on Nintendo Switch Online, but there isn't even a library for the console.

title: Japanese Charts: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Physical Takes The Lion's Share Of Its Japanese Sales
summary:
Physical is dead, eh?

After Nintendo's reveal this week that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time had shifted 5.2 million units in its first four days, it will come as no surprise to hear that it's a smash hit in Japan. But still, Famitsu's latest numbers are in, and the physical is flying!

According to this week's chart, Link's latest produced ~537,000 physical sales in its chart debut — giving it the lion's share of Japan's 810,000 sales that Nintendo reported, and leaving around 273,000 sales for digital. As we say, it's hardly surprising, but still!
